title: Institutional Transitions: Pasar a in Legislative Discourse

sections.content:
You know *pasar a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 23 for moving on to the next step (*pasemos a ver*) or changing role (*pasó a dirigir*). Legislative reports and civic speeches use *pasar a* in three formal institutional frames.

1. **Procedural transitions with passive infinitives:** a bill or measure moves from one stage to the next with *pasar a ser* + agreeing participle: *El proyecto de ley pasa a ser examinado por la comisión*; *La derogación pasó a ser votada en el pleno*.
2. **Institutional reassignment:** fixed phrases express a change of status or authority: *pasar a formar parte de* ('to become part of') and *pasar a depender de* ('to come under the authority of'): *La oficina pasó a depender del consejo para reforzar la separación de poderes*.
3. **Agenda shifts in a speech:** *pasemos a* + infinitive (*pasemos a examinar*, *pasemos a abordar*) moves an assembly politely from one topic to the next.

sections.title: pasar a in legislative and institutional speech
rows: El proyecto de ley pasa a ser revisado por la comisión técnica.
Tras el veto, la norma pasó a debatirse de nuevo en el pleno.
Sequential shift after a prior institutional step.
La oficina pasó a depender de un organismo independiente.
Pasemos a examinar las prioridades de esta nueva legislatura.
1st-person plural subjunctive: moving the agenda forward.

items.spanish: Una vez aprobado en comisión, el proyecto de ley pasa a ser debatido en el pleno de la legislatura.
items.english: Once approved in committee, the bill moves on to be debated in the full session of the legislative term.

items.spanish: Tras la derogación del reglamento anterior, las normas nuevas pasaron a formar parte del código local.
items.english: Following the repeal of the previous regulation, the new rules became part of the local code.

items.spanish: En respeto a la separación de poderes, el control presupuestario pasó a depender de una junta independiente.
items.english: Out of respect for the separation of powers, budget oversight came under an independent board.

items.spanish: Pasemos ahora a analizar cómo legislar con mayor transparencia frente a un posible veto.
items.english: Let us move on now to analyse how to legislate with greater transparency in the face of a possible veto.

sections.content: Always keep the preposition *a* after *pasar* (*pasa a ser debatido*, *pasemos a examinar*), and remember that *pasar a* marks a step that follows an earlier stage—never use it for a brand-new beginning where nothing came before (there, use *empezar a* or *comenzar a*).
